title: Tom Holland's Best Spider-Man Performance Yet
review:
Spider-Man: Brand New Day is a really interesting entry into Tom Holland's Spider-Man run because, in my opinion, this is easily his best performance as Peter Parker so far. Holland feels more comfortable in the role than ever, and there's a lot more emotional weight behind his performance. You can really feel what Peter is going through, and it gives the character a much stronger presence.

The movie also looks fantastic. The visuals are impressive, and the action is easily one of the biggest strengths. There are some really creative sequences here, and when Spider-Man starts doing Spider-Man things, the movie absolutely delivers. The character dynamics are another highlight, with some genuinely fun interactions that give the film a lot of personality.

The soundtrack also deserves some praise. It fits the movie really well and adds a lot to the bigger moments without constantly screaming "THIS IS AN IMPORTANT SCENE." The dialogue is also surprisingly strong for the most part. There are some genuinely good conversations between the characters, and the movie gives them enough room to actually interact instead of just jumping from action scene to action scene.

The story is where things get a little more complicated for me.

The first two arcs are really strong. They build the story nicely, develop the characters, and kept me invested in what was happening. The pacing during these parts works really well, and I was genuinely enjoying where the movie was going.

Then the third act happens...

And that's where I started losing interest.

The main antagonist just doesn't work particularly well for me. I never found them especially compelling, and the way the conflict is resolved feels much weaker than what the first two acts had built toward. After spending so much time being invested in the story, I expected the final part to really bring everything together, but instead it felt like the movie was slowly losing steam.

By the end, I actually noticed myself thinking, "Okay, I kind of just want this to be over now." And that's never a great sign. It's not that the third act is completely terrible, but compared to how much I enjoyed the first two, it definitely feels like a step down.

Still, Spider-Man: Brand New Day has a lot going for it. Tom Holland gives what I consider his strongest Spider-Man performance, the visuals and action are excellent, the character dynamics are enjoyable, and the soundtrack and dialogue work really well.

title: For that Kid inside You...

So finally after so many days I saw something great, something appreciable, something that will force you to sit and see it all at once. Something which I call "great". Thank You Very Much, Sadie Ji for keeping the love inside me still alive.

And that Convo between Peter & MJ... That really felt like an ache, a sweet ache, an ache that I really needed for keeping the spark of love inside me alive. The ache the forced tears to come into my eyes but sweet and hitting enough to not let those tears roll down my eyes coz' you know that just like Peter, things aren't gonna change... You have to live with it coz' that's the cost you pay for being Spider-Man! And Tom Holland, thank you for reminding why I need to be a good guy, a nice kid. I know I never was, but from this point on, I will try coz' that's what Spidey do, he try till he die and from now on, I will be a nice kid, once again! (yeah, you heard it right). Back when I was 12th I really used to get pissed off whenever people said "you are a nice guy" to me coz' at that time I had this mindset that nice guys end up with nothing. But it's today I realised that the world needs nice kids! Kids who know how to sacrifice, kids who know how to love, kids who know how to live for others, and I will be one of them.

Coming to the writing and direction part, I would say not anything in this movie feels overdone, or underdone, or even misplaced. The emotional scenes, the pain, the joy, those tiny crumbs of laughter, they sprinkled them very respectively and politely in between, all of it feels as one of the very perfect mix I've seen in a movie after like years! Everything feels exactly the way it should. The way I'd want my own story to feel if I ever wrote one with complete honesty, with all my heart and soul! That's how Brand New Day feels - Not perfect, but just right! Right enough to be loved, to be experienced, to be lived & appreciated and to be always kept in good books. And if needed, gatekeep it to ;) Now if you're going to watch this movie just for, you know, No Way Home type sh!t, a lot of actions and all, then surely you wouldn't get it but if you're going to watch it for the sake of cinema, for the love of Marvel, then trust me, you'll regard this as one of the best masterpiece made by Marvel in years! The Classic Hulk transformation, the og web swinging, I missed them so much. It felt like rediscovering a part of myself that I had lost long ago. A part I didn't even realise was missing until this movie somehow brought it back.

And at the end I would just say, this movie deserves to be watched in a cinema, to be respected and enjoyed with friends & lovers or even yourself. So don't pirate it or spoil it coz' there are many things in this movie which can only be felt by seeing it, by heart, by mind, by soul. Respect the makers, respect the cinema, and if you're one of them who's first superhero movie was Spider-Man, then respect that kid inside yours too! He/she needs it. You may don't know, but trust me, that kid needs it more than you do. And hear me out, when the movie will end, that kid inside you would just wish that it should've never ended coz' this movie will become the reason for that kid to be alive again, to be stress free again, to actually be happy again!

So go & watch for that kid and love the cinema the way it is!

title: Scrams comic book
review:
Peter Parker has been forgotten, so he now concentrates solely on being SPIDER-MAN. But as the loneliness starts taking a toll, a new threat appears, further complicating things for our hero.

We've now had ten years of Tom Holland as SPIDER-MAN, with BRAND NEW DAY being the fourth solo film, and there's no indication of things slowing down. In fact, this is some of the best we've gotten from the character.

This movie screams comic book! It absolutely has the look and feel of one, with visuals and scenes pulled right out of the pages. But it's not only about the looks-it's the overall substance as well. It's packed with characters who all feel organic rather than forced. You get that built-up, lived-in world that's been around for a while, and the movie pulls it off very nicely. Every character has a purpose that drives the story forward. I especially liked the scenes where they show SPIDER-MAN taking on villains over the years. It did a great job showing how much time had passed and how much of Peter's life had become being SPIDER-MAN, and how little he had left outside of the mask.

The action looks awesome! And the suit... I totally loved the look of it. It felt real! Not something that's all digital, but something the actor is actually wearing. It's one of the best on-screen SPIDER-MAN suits, in my opinion. At times you can even see Peter's eyes through the SPIDER-MAN mask, which was a nice touch that added to the realism.

Story-wise, I feel they handled the aftermath of NO WAY HOME perfectly. You really feel Peter's loneliness, and it plays a huge part in the movie. Everything involving MJ and Ned was fantastic. All three have such great chemistry, and they're the emotional backbone of the film.

The whole cast delivers and works really well together. Returning are Tom Holland, Zendaya, Jacob Batalon, Marisa Tomei, and Michael Mando, while newcomers Jon Bernthal, Mark Ruffalo, Florence Pugh, Sadie Sink, Liza Colón-Zayas, and Tramell Tillman fit right in.

BRAND NEW DAY felt like a movie set within a huge cinematic universe, but I also liked that it focused on telling one smaller-scale story. Having characters from other films and shows come and go was a brilliant idea that gave it that comic book feel. Destin Daniel Cretton nailed it! Everything here just worked.

I had a blast! The theater was packed, and everyone was locked in. It's a must-see movie! Go check it out!

SPIDER-MAN is truly one of the best characters ever created... I hope they keep going with this version for at least another two solo films.

title: Spider-Man Finally Home
review:
Going into Spider-Man: Brand New Day, I expected to enjoy it, but I wasn't prepared for how much I would genuinely love it. What surprised me most wasn't just how good the movie was, but the reason it worked so well for me: Tom Holland finally feels like Spider-Man.

Not just Peter Parker. Spider-Man.

This movie gives us more time to see him truly embrace what makes the character special. The humor, the awkwardness, the kindness, and the responsibility all come together in a way that feels like a reminder of why Spider-Man has remained one of the most beloved superheroes of all time.

The biggest moments weren't necessarily the action sequences. It was the smaller, quieter scenes that stood out the most. Watching Peter interact with people, make jokes, struggle, and simply try to do the right thing reminded me that Spider-Man has always been at his best when he's the friendly neighborhood hero. This movie understands that and gives those moments the time they deserve.

The action is exciting, the comedy feels natural, and the emotional moments actually land. The movie manages to be fun, heartfelt, and surprisingly moving without losing sight of what makes Spider-Man special.

For me, No Way Home was a love letter to Spider-Man fans. It celebrated everything the character has been and honored the history behind him. Brand New Day feels like a love letter to Spider-Man himself. It reminded me why I fell in love with the character in the first place. The humor, the heart, the responsibility, and the simple idea of a hero who is always there to help, no matter what.

I walked out with a huge smile on my face. This is the Spider-Man I've been waiting to see.

title: A Missed Opportunity for Both Spider-Man and Jean
review:
I would give this film a 5 out of 10. Overall, it felt like a missed opportunity that doesn't add much value to the broader Marvel Cinematic Universe or the upcoming Avengers storyline.

My biggest issue with the movie is the strange shift in focus. While watching, it felt less like a Spider-Man movie and more like a setup for Jean. Given how crucial Jean is going to be in future Avengers films, introducing and developing such an important character inside a Spider-Man solo movie does a disservice to both sides. Jean genuinely deserves her own standalone film or TV series. Shoving her arc into this plot ended up hurting the movie's pacing while failing to give Jean the proper solo spotlight she merits.

Additionally, the portrayal of the villains was quite disappointing. We barely saw anything beyond what was already revealed in the trailers, which was a huge letdown.

The movie clearly tried to focus on a deeper psychological aspect alongside Jean's introduction, but unfortunately, it failed to deliver on both fronts. It didn't land the psychological depth effectively, nor did it give Jean the shine she deserved. A standalone project for Jean would have been a much better decision.

title: A familiar but somewhat of a brand new day
review: Spiderman:a brand new day is the newest installment in MCU. The last film No Way Home, was a nostalgic trip, but still a great addition to Spider-Man's growth as a character, dealing with actual risk and the sacrifices of being a hero. Going into this film, I wasn't all that impressed by the trailer, so I tampered my expectations. And after seeing it, I can say it was enjoyable. The biggest positive is the overall look of the film (for the most part ) is pretty good. The previous three films, (while not awful looking ) really lacked in its own unique style. In this film I would say about 85-90% of the shots are very interesting. The web swinging and action in particular. There's some really cool over the shoulder shots that almost feel you are on Spider-Man's back while he's swinging. There's a specific action scene in a cell with the Hand that involves team synced based attacks and is really well coordinated and in never feels super claustrophobic. The acting from everyone is also pretty good. Tom Holland still really works as spider man. He has some emotional moments in the film and they work well. I also really like the first half of the film. While it has been done before In Spiderman 2 , I like the idea of actually getting into Peter's mind, and they do some cool sound and visual design choices, to make you feel the stress and isolation that he's feeling. The biggest negative is that the plot is predictable. There's a reveal of who's the villain and while it's not bad, as the story goes along it becomes more obvious where they're going with it. There are some really notable bad effects. While I did say that most of the effects are good, they're are some scenes with some really noticeable green screen and some characters designs ( while not in the movie for long) just didn't translate well to the screen. I also think the movie should've been about 5 to 10 minutes shorter. Their is a big thing that happens and I feel they ended on a certain shot, it would've left a lot more of an emotional impact. Spiderman: a brand new day is a solid follow up to no way home. While it can have some weak visual effects and a second half that is not as strong as the first, it's still a fun time, while also progressing Peter's character arc of dealing with grief and loss. I do hope this director does another Spider-Man film with Tom holland, with some tweaks and improvements, he could make a really great spider man movie.
